extractions.title: Guidance on the Assurance of Machine Learning in Autonomous Systems (AMLAS)
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3.2 (ML Verification Assurance), pp. 24-38; Stage 5 (Model Verification)
extractions.input_requirements_format: High-level ML safety requirements and operating domain constraints formulated in GSN.
extractions.evidence_source: Internally collected test sets, verification test logs, and performance metrics generated during the internal ML lifecycle.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Assumes end-to-end development logging; uncollected verification evidence causes assurance stage transition failure.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Binary safety claim argument acceptance based on meeting internal verification thresholds.
extractions.delineation_gap: Focuses strictly on internal ML development pipelines; does not provide a decision calculus for qualifying third-party benchmark evidence or managing external test deficits.

extractions.title: Assurance Contracts for Component-Based Systems: Reusing Safety Cases
extractions.input_requirements_format: Assumption-guarantee contracts specifying deterministic interface requirements and operating assumptions.
extractions.evidence_source: Component vendor safety cases, static analysis proofs, and formal verification tests.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Unsatisfied assumptions invalidate the guarantee; contract remains unfulfilled.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Deductive logical composition; guarantees hold if all system-level assumptions are formally satisfied.
extractions.delineation_gap: Assumes deterministic, modular software components with provable contracts; lacks statistical confidence bounding or epistemic audit gates for generative AI benchmarks.

extractions.title: Safety Case Impact Assessment in Automotive Software Systems: An Improved Model Based Approach
extractions.input_requirements_format: Structured GSN safety claims linked to architectural models and implementation artifacts.
extractions.evidence_source: Code modification diffs, change manifests, and regression test suites.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Modified artifacts with unverified impact are flagged for re-assurance and cannot be admitted.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Traceability graph traversal identifying safety arguments invalidated by upstream software changes.
extractions.delineation_gap: Addresses maintenance and regression across known internal code modifications; does not address initial evidence qualification for third-party foundation models.

extractions.title: Transfer Assurance: Reusing Safety Cases Across Operational Contexts
extractions.section_evidence: Section 2 (Transfer Assurance Argument Pattern), SafeAI pp. 1-8
extractions.input_requirements_format: Operational Domain Specifications (ODDs) with parametric environmental boundaries.
extractions.evidence_source: Empirical test distributions and statistical distance metrics across perceptual robot domains.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Unmeasured domain divergence leaves the transfer argument unsupported.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Quantification of domain shift via statistical divergence; justifies claim validity across context transfers.
extractions.delineation_gap: Designed for perceptual robotic distribution shift (lighting, weather); does not address discrete software engineering tasks, coding benchmarks, or test oracle validity.

extractions.title: VNVSpec: A Machine-Readable Specification Language for AI Verification and Validation
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3 (DSL Syntax and Semantic Execution Engine), pp. 45-56
extractions.input_requirements_format: Declarative Domain-Specific Language (DSL) defining operational requirements, test bounds, and acceptance assertions.
extractions.evidence_source: Automated execution traces against internally hosted test harnesses.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Unasserted requirements remain explicitly marked as unverified.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Compiles machine-readable requirements into automated executable test suites.
extractions.delineation_gap: Executes internal test suites directly against local models; lacks mechanisms to evaluate the evidentiary validity or oracle deficits of external third-party benchmarks.

extractions.title: Reusing Assurance Evidence in AI Pipelines: Validity Conditions, a Fail-Closed Release Gate, and a Replay of 714 Public Data Version Control Pipelines
extractions.section_evidence: Sections 3 & 4 (Validity Conditions and Release Gate Architecture), Section 5 (DVC Pipeline Replay), pp. 1-18
extractions.input_requirements_format: Declared pipeline stage dependencies and governance release policy assertions.
extractions.evidence_source: Signed execution traces, stage outputs, and Git/DVC dependency hashes across pipeline revisions.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Undeclared or changed dependencies invalidate reused stage outputs, forcing fail-closed stage re-execution.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Cryptographically signed release gate enforcing fail-closed re-execution when candidate dependencies diverge from signed evidence.
extractions.delineation_gap: Focuses on internal pipeline re-execution and dependency invalidation in MLOps/DVC workflows; does not evaluate third-party benchmark construct validity, oracle correctness, or requirements satisfaction across external models.

extractions.title: Assurance Envelopes for Autonomous Coding Agents: Minimum-Cost Evidence for Software Change
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3 (Inference Graphs and Minimum-Cost Envelopes), Section 4 (CP-SAT Solver Validation), pp. 1-15
extractions.input_requirements_format: Preserved software properties and change obligations formulated over typed inference graphs.
extractions.evidence_source: Accumulated software artifacts from prior coding-agent runs (tests, type checks, formal proofs, static analysis traces).
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: If available evidence cannot re-establish an obligation closure, no valid envelope exists; triggers complete re-verification.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Forward chaining over typed inference graphs paired with CP-SAT constraint optimization to select the least-cost subset of prior evidence.
extractions.delineation_gap: Focuses on selecting minimum-cost prior internal verification evidence to restore properties during software maintenance; leaves obligation discovery open and does not address design-time requirements acceptance using external benchmark scores.

authors: National Institute of Standards and Technology
extractions.title: Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models
extractions.section_evidence: Section 4 (Benchmark Quality and Contamination Management), NIST AI 800-2 ipd, pp. 18-32
extractions.input_requirements_format: General risk management goals and governance requirements (NIST AI RMF).
extractions.evidence_source: Public benchmark leaderboards, standardized test harnesses, and model evaluation reports.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Recommends reporting missing evaluation metadata; disclaims binary acceptance rules.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Qualitative institutional governance recommendations and reporting checklists.
extractions.delineation_gap: Provides institutional governance guidance; lacks an executable decision calculus or formal mapping from benchmark scores to software system requirements.

extractions.title: What the Specification Did Not Say: Specification-Oracle Gaps in Test-Graded Coding-Agent Benchmarks
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3 (Taxonomy of Oracle Flaws) & Section 5 (Empirical Discrepancy Findings), arXiv:2610.30635
extractions.input_requirements_format: Natural language prompt docstrings in code benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, SWE-bench).
extractions.evidence_source: Hidden unit test suites and execution logs across code generation models.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Identifies over-constrained hidden testcases that penalize correct code with false failures.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Automated AST and execution mutation testing isolating test oracle defects.
extractions.delineation_gap: Audits benchmark test defects in isolation; does not formulate a requirements engineering method to decide whether defective or sound benchmarks support system requirements.

extractions.title: Large Language Models for Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
extractions.section_evidence: Section 5 (Model Evaluation and Benchmarking Practices in SE), pp. 45-62
extractions.input_requirements_format: Software engineering task descriptions (code repair, test generation, documentation).
extractions.evidence_source: Empirical pass rates compiled from literature across diverse SE benchmarks.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Notes widespread reporting gaps; treats missing details as threats to study validity.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Literature synthesis comparing relative model rankings across SE tasks.
extractions.delineation_gap: Surveys general model capability rankings; does not provide an operational evidence qualification calculus for requirements engineers.

extractions.title: From Model Proliferation to Deployment Intelligence: A Risk-Traceable System-Aware Model Selection Framework
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3 (System-Aware Model Selection Architecture) & Section 4 (DAMSA Implementation), pp. 1-24
extractions.input_requirements_format: Risk-traceable operational requirements and multi-attribute deployment constraints (latency, cost, hardware limits).
extractions.evidence_source: Empirical model evaluation metrics across operational hazard test suites and multi-objective performance benchmarks.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Models failing mandatory constraints or lacking verified risk metrics are filtered during candidate-control screening.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Three-layer decision architecture: Pre-Ranking criteria translation, DAMSA Pareto screening and reference ranking, and Post-Ranking perturbation/robustness analysis.
extractions.delineation_gap: Focuses on multi-attribute post-training deployment selection for predictive ML models; does not evaluate generative coding agent benchmarks, test oracle validity, or formalize requirements satisfaction using confidence intervals and meta-evaluation admissibility gates.

extractions.title: ECBD: Evidence-Centered Benchmark Design for NLP
extractions.section_evidence: Section 3 (ECBD Modules: Capability, Content, Adaptation, Assembly, Evidence) & Appendix A (Worksheet)
extractions.input_requirements_format: Intended benchmark use specifications and linguistic capability constructs.
extractions.evidence_source: NLP benchmark design choices, item pools, and model response scoring rubrics.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Worksheet flags unjustified design choices and missing validity evidence as threats to validity.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Evidence-centered design guidance prompting benchmark creators to describe, justify, and support choices.
extractions.delineation_gap: Guides the authoring and construct validation of NLP benchmarks; does not provide an automated decision calculus for software requirements engineers reusing benchmark scores.

extractions.title: BetterBench: Assessing AI Benchmarks, Uncovering Issues, and Establishing Best Practices
extractions.section_evidence: Sections 3-5 (Quality Criteria: Construct Validity, Test Quality, Data Quality, Infrastructure), pp. 1-18
extractions.input_requirements_format: AI benchmark evaluation rubrics and quality checklists.
extractions.evidence_source: Benchmark repositories, dataset inspection, implementation code, and reproducibility audits.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Assigns zero/penalty scores to criteria lacking documented evidence or open code.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Comprehensive multi-attribute quality scoring across 15 benchmark dimensions.
extractions.delineation_gap: Evaluates overall benchmark artifact quality and engineering hygiene; does not link benchmark results to specific system requirements or determine requirement satisfaction.

extractions.title: Evaluation Cards: An Interpretive Layer for AI Evaluation Reporting
extractions.section_evidence: Sections 2 & 3 (Interpretive Layer & Audience-Specific Views), arXiv:2606.09809, pp. 1-14
extractions.input_requirements_format: Standardized evaluation reporting schemas tailored to diverse stakeholder personas.
extractions.evidence_source: Benchmark evaluation metadata, task descriptions, test parameters, and limitation disclosures.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Displays documentation gaps and omitted parameters visually in reporting cards.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Structured qualitative reporting layer improving evaluation interpretability.
extractions.delineation_gap: Improves qualitative reporting transparency for human readers; lacks formal decision thresholds, statistical bounding, or automated requirements acceptance logic.

extractions.title: Beyond the Hype: Enabling Informed LLM Adoption in Industry through Systematic Evaluation
extractions.section_evidence: Science of Computer Programming 254:103530, Sections 3 & 4 (Systematic Evaluation and Industrial Adoption), pp. 1-18
extractions.input_requirements_format: Critical epistemological and empirical evaluation of AI benchmarking for industry adoption.
extractions.evidence_source: Systematic evaluation datasets, industrial adoption criteria, and benchmark limitation audits.
extractions.missing_evidence_rule: Identifies unverified leaderboard pass rates and benchmark saturation as insufficient evidence for deployment.
extractions.decision_mechanics: Systematic evaluation methodology guiding industry stakeholders beyond leaderboard scores.
extractions.delineation_gap: Provides an informed evaluation framework for industrial LLM adoption; does not formulate a requirements engineering decision calculus with statistical confidence bounds or Kane admissibility gates for code generation.
